what: Knee — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps. A rep that pauses at the top is still "reps" — add "repHold".
fields.repHold: Optional, reps only: seconds the top of each rep must be held before it counts, e.g. 2. The counter only counts a rep once the reading has stayed at the target for that long; reach the top and come straight back down and it is a partial, with the built-in "shortHold" fault ("Hold it there") explaining why. The coach shows the hold ticking down at the top and chimes when it is up. Good: 1–3 s. Bad: 10 s (that is a timed hold — use type "hold").
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.listed: Whether the move is offered in the lists people browse — the home page and Moves. Left out it follows "vetted", so a library that grows faster than anyone can check it does not bury the moves that were checked. true shows one that is not vetted yet; false hides one that is. Hiding is about browsing only: a routine that names the move still runs it, and a link straight to it still opens. Good: true once a physio has been through it with you. Bad: true on everything, which is the same as no shortlist at all.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". A movement measured by more than one angle takes "and": a list of further measurements, each with its own "metric", "start" and "target" — a squat is the knee bending AND the hip folding, and a rep that does one without the other is not the exercise. "combine" says how they become one number: "min" (the default — the rep is only as far through as its least-finished part), "mean" or "max". The first measurement stays the one the readout shows and the target line is drawn for. Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number. A movement can also have a far end: "max" is where the joint starts working outside the range the exercise is for. Write it as a number, or as { "delta": n } — a distance past the target, which follows the person’s own choice when they pick their range. It compiles into a built-in fault, "past_range" (an id no move may use), so the far end is not a second hand-written copy of the progress measurement that has to be kept in step with the first. "overLabel", "overCue" (≤ 8 words) and "overTip" put your own words on it, "overSeverity" (1–3) and "overInvalidates" set how it scores. Optional: plenty of movements have no far end. Good: a knee extension that should not be forced past straight. Bad: a far end nearer the start than the target, which every rep trips the moment it counts.
fields.show: What the coach asks the person to demonstrate once, before the set, so the target is measured on their body instead of assumed: { "ask": "arms straight out to the sides, level with your shoulders, nothing in your hands" }. They hold that pose still for a moment, with the band or weight out of the way, and what it reads becomes progress.target for the set. Only for a counted move, and only worth it when the number in progress.target depends on the body or the angle — a raise to shoulder height, a hands-apart distance — or when the equipment hides the joints. progress.target is still required: it is the fallback, and the sanity check (a demonstration under 40% or over 250% of it is refused). Good: one short sentence naming the end position. Bad: "do the exercise".
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps), "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position), or "start" — read once on the start position before the set, for a set-up error that is unfixable later (heels too far away, knee already bent, band already taut); a start check may not be a rule and may not use "rel": "change", since the start is what it is judging. "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.stable: Optional: the landmarks that do not move during this exercise, e.g. ["SH", "KNEE"] for a bridge, where the hip rises between a shoulder and a knee that stay on the floor. The target line drawn over the camera is pinned to them: told which end is still, it does not have to guess from how far each end has moved so far, and it cannot guess wrong on the first rep. They are also held still on the drawn skeleton once they have stopped moving — the pose model’s guess for a planted foot or a resting shoulder wanders a couple of pixels a frame, and a point that is known not to move is better held than followed — and let go the moment they plainly move. A point a fault watches for its own movement (a heel that must not lift, a toe that must stay down) is never held. Name them the way a measurement does (SH, HIP, KNEE, oKNEE…). Leave it out and the coach works it out by watching. Good: the one or two points the person is resting on. Bad: listing every point (nothing is left to draw the target for).
fields.cues: Optional: what the coach says on its own account, and when. A block of stage: setting, where the setting is false to say nothing at that moment, or the words to say in place of the usual ones (for "praise" and "mark", a list). Stages, in the order a set meets them: "opening" (the brief as the camera opens), "position" (get into frame), "start" (the set-up faults read before the count-in), "show" (asking for the end position), "countIn" (3, 2, 1), "go", "count" (the number after each rep), "praise" (the word after a clean one — a list to draw from), "partial" (the line after a rep that did not count), "fault" (the live fault cues), "mark" (a hold’s halfway and countdown — a list of seconds), "enter" (get into the hold position), "finish" (the summary), "lost", "turn". A stage left out behaves as it always did. Good: { "count": false, "praise": ["Steady"] } on a twenty-rep set nobody wants counted aloud. Bad: silencing "fault" on a move whose whole point is the form.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.weight: Optional, the alternative to a band: a hand-weight bubble in kilograms. "none", 1, 2 or 5 = offers it with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none. The steps come from settings.json (weight) and the last one, Other…, lets the person type any weight. A move may offer both a band and a weight.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.
fields.farSide: Optional, side-on moves worked with both sides at once: "ignore" leaves the arm and leg away from the camera out of it. Behind the body they are a guess, and on a move that works both sides together they say nothing the near limb does not. Ignored, they are not drawn on the skeleton, not required in frame before a set can start, and — checked when the move is compiled — not measured: a progress metric, hold condition or fault naming oKNEE, oANK, oHEEL, oFOOT, oEL or oWR is refused. The torso pairs are not the far side in this sense: both shoulders and both hips are what the trunk is read from and both stay visible, so oSH and oHIP are still yours to use. Good: a bridge, a plank, a squat filmed side-on. Bad: on a one-sided move (it already names the limb it works) or a face-on one (neither limb is the far one).
